chunks: Sulaimān ibn Khālid asked him about a man who cuts from the arāk tree that is in Makkah. He said:
He is liable for its value, which he gives in charity, and nothing should be removed from the trees of Makkah except palm trees and fruit trees.

key_terms.الْأَرَاكِ: the arāk tree mentioned as the tree being cut in Makkah
key_terms.ثَمَنُهُ: its monetary value, which becomes due as compensation
key_terms.شَجَرِ مَكَّةَ: the trees of Makkah, whose removal is generally prohibited

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting trees in Makkah according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning cutting trees in Makkah, indicating that doing so entails financial liability to be given as charity. It also establishes an exception for palm trees and fruit trees, reflecting the sanctity and protected status of the vegetation of Makkah.
